paragraphs: Rabbi Oshaya and Rabbi Yehudah Nesia at Rav Yehudah’s doorway. (Bava Kamma 19b reads Rabbi Yehudah—an error; it should be Rav Yehudah.) Perhaps this is Rabbi Oshaya the great, who lived long, until Rav Yehudah’s days. Yet Hamafkid 43b: Rabbi Oshaya tells Rav Yehudah, “Master, do you say so?”—“Thus said Rabbi Assi in Rabbi Yochanan’s name.” This appears not to be Oshaya the great. Beginning of Kol Haget 25a: he asked Rabbi Yehudah, who replied, “Oshaya my son, what have Passover offerings to do with this?” (Hachovel 88, beginning of b: Rabbi Abba said it before Rabbi Hoshaya, who went and said it before Rav Yehudah; he answered, “Thus said Shmuel.”) Tosafot, Yevamot 19a: Oshaya at the end of Yom Tov 37 and at 10 is not Oshaya in Haddar. They distinguish Rav Oshaya and Rabbi Oshaya; a Rav Oshaya in the later amoraic days asked Rav Yehudah, as Tosafot, Haddar 68a, likewise state. Moreover, how was he in Babylonia? Who places Rabbi Yehudah Nesia there, at Rav Yehudah’s doorway? Perhaps he once went there, or Rav Yehudah went to the Land of Israel (see Rachava). Megillah 7, end of a: Rabbi Yehudah Nesia sent to Rabbi Oshaya. Jerusalem Talmud, Megillah, chapter 1, halakhah 6: Rabbi Yudan Nesia sent Rabbi Oshaya the great a calf’s thigh, etc.; he replied, “Our master, you have fulfilled through us,” etc. This suggests Oshaya was Rabbi Yehudah Nesia’s student. I find it difficult for several reasons to make Oshaya the great his student. Jerusalem Talmud, end of the first chapter of Beitzah, halakhah 11: Oshaya the great asks Yehudah Nesia, “Did you hear from your father that a hen may be moved?” He answers in a whisper. “Why do you tell me in a whisper?” “As I heard it in a whisper, so I tell you.” If he were his teacher, he should have said “Did the master” or “Rabbi hear from your father?” Why not “Rabbi told me in a whisper”? Mo'ed Katan has Yehudah Nesia alive when Rav Yehudah died; see there and the first chapter. In my view necessity is not blameworthy: there were two Yehudah Nesias (as I wrote there) and two Oshayas. The second of each stood at Rav Yehudah’s doorway; the second Rav Oshaya called the second Yehudah Nesia “master.” Oshaya the great asked the first Yehudah Nesia “Did you hear from your father?” because he was not his teacher. The second Yehudah Nesia was alive at Rav Yehudah’s death. This explains many confusions. Perhaps Tosafot’s Rav/Rabbi distinction is necessary because chronology yields two Rav Oshayas: so I thought. But Jerusalem Talmud, Megillah, above, says Yudan Nesia sent to Oshaya the great, and thus this explanation cannot stand.
